Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And

Judgment:
(Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili) Heard the learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer.

2. This Appeal, under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short, 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer challenging the order and decree dated 02.11.2006 passed in O.P.No.63 of 2000 by the learned Senior Civil Judge, Jagitial (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court").
3.

The brief facts of the case are that an extent of land admeasuring Ac.2-08 gts in Sy.No.767/B situated at Dharmapuri Village, Jagityal District, belonging to the respondents/claimants, was acquired for the purpose of providing house sites to flood victims; that draft notification under Section 4 (1) of the Act and declaration under Section 6 of the Act were published ::2:: AKS,J &
LNA,J in the A.P. Gazette on 12.01.1996 and 13.01.1996, respectively; that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary enquiry, passed Award dated 30.04.1997, granting compensation of Rs.8,000/- per acre to the respondents/claimants for the acquired lands.
4. Not being satisfied with the Award, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was numbered as O.P.No.63 of 2000 on the file of the Reference Court.
5.
Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.Ws.1 to 3 were examined and Ex.A1 (certified copy of registered sale deed, dated 31.12.1998) was marked.

On behalf of the Land Acquisition Officer, RW-1 was examined and Ex.B1 (Award proceedings, dated 30.04.1997)
was marked.

6. The Reference Court, on appreciation of the entire evidence and material available on record,
passed the impugned order enhancing the market value of the acquired lands to Rs.50,000/- per acre from ::3:: AKS,J & LNA,J Rs.8,000/- per acre, apart from granting other benefits under the Act to the respondents/claimants.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the impugned order, dated 02.11.2006 passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.

8. Learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant had contended that the Reference Court has erred in relying upon Ex.A1-the registered sale deed, which is seven (7) years prior to the date of issuance of draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act.
The Reference Court erred in enhancing the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, and therefore, prayed to set aside the impugned order passed by the Reference Court.

9. A perusal of the record discloses that the land acquired is very near to National Highway-16,
which is running from Nizamabad to Jagadalpur.

The said land is situated at Dharmapuri Village,
which is a holy place to which pilgrims from all over India visit to have darshan.
The Land Acquisition Officer has verified ::4:: AKS,J & LNA,J altogether 59 registered sale transactions, which took place from 1993 to 1995.

However, he has discarded all the transactions on the ground that the sale transactions were in respect of small extents and also for commercial purpose, except the sale transactions at SI.No.39 and 40, whereby lands in Sy.Nos.283/C and 283/A, were sold @
Rs.8,000/- per acre.

10. The Reference Court has relied on Ex.A1 i.e., certified copy of the registered sale deed, dated 31.12.1998 under which an extent of Ac.0.26 gts of land was sold for Rs.1,26,000/- per acre from the same survey number.

The Reference Court has also observed that certain sale transactions took place from 1993 to 1995 and as per these transactions, lands which are very near to the acquired land were sold @ Rs.20,000/- per acre to Rs.7,26,000/- per acre.

11. The Reference Court has considered Ex.A1- registered sale deed, dated 31.12.1998 as a basis for enhancement of market value of the acquired land, since the said sale transaction pertains to the same ::5:: AKS,J & LNA,J survey number and determined the market value @ Rs.50,000/- per acre,
on the ground that the claimant has initially agreed to part with his land for Rs.50,000/- per acre.
However, there are transactions through which similar lands were sold @ Rs.1,00,000/- per acre.
It is also observed that even if 1/3rd of the said amount is deducted, still the respondents/claimants would be entitled to Rs.50,000/- per acre.
12. In the light of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Reference Court was justified in enhancing the market value from Rs.8,000/- per acre to Rs.50,000/- per acre, since,
Ex .A1-registered sale deed pertains to same survey number and was executed seven years prior to the date of draft notification under Section 4 (1) of the Act.
Therefore, this Court does not find any illegality or irregularity in the impugned order passed by the Reference Court.
::6:: AKS,J & LNA,J 13.
The Appeal is accordingly, dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
